title: Relative monoidal tuple cones with prescribed color values
statement: Use a monoidal infinity category $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the inert color projections $\rho_i:[n]\to[1]$ as in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], and relative limit diagrams on join cones as in [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Fix $n\geq0$, let $I$ be the discrete simplicial set on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $g:I^{\triangleleft}\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ have apex $[n]$, all boundary values $[1]$, and edges $\rho_i$. For any prescribed objects $v_i\in\mathcal V=\mathcal V^\otimes_{[1]}$, there exists a cone $q:I^{\triangleleft}\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ whose boundary is exactly $(v_i)$, with $pq=g$, and whose edges are $p$-cocartesian. For every specified cone $q$ with this boundary and base, $q$ is a $p$-limit diagram if and only if each edge $q(*)\to v_i$ is $p$-cocartesian. These assertions include $n=0$: the boundary is empty, the apex lies over $[0]$, and every such empty cone is a $p$-limit diagram. No ordinary limits, colimits or presentability of $\mathcal V$ are assumed.

proof.text: An equivalence edge $u:x\to y$ over an identity of the base is $p$-cocartesian. Indeed its inverse and inverse triangles make precomposition $\operatorname{Map}(y,z)\to\operatorname{Map}(x,z)$ a homotopy equivalence for each $z$, by the composition statement [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. The corresponding lower map of base mapping spaces is the identity. Its path pullback is equivalent to the upper-right space (contract the path coordinate), so the square is a homotopy pullback. The criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] gives the assertion.

source.place: Elementary use of the cocartesian mapping criterion and inverse triangles; GH Definition 3.1.3, exact-boundary preparation.

proof.text: Choose a Segal transport equivalence $T:\mathcal V^\otimes_{[n]}\to\mathcal V^n$ from [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. Apply a quasi-inverse of $T$ to the prescribed tuple to obtain $C$, with a tuple equivalence $T(C)\simeq(v_i)$. Write the chosen transport edges as $e_i:C\to w_i$ over $\rho_i$; their existence is part of the cocartesian-fibration definition. Projecting the tuple equivalence and its inverse triangles to each coordinate gives equivalences $u_i:w_i\to v_i$ in the fiber over $[1]$. These are cocartesian by Step 1. Fill the inner $2$-horn $(e_i,u_i)$ over the composable pair $(\rho_i,1_{[1]})$; let its long edge be $a_i:C\to v_i$. The composition assertion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] makes $a_i$ cocartesian. Its base is exactly $\rho_i$. The left cone on discrete $I$ is the union of these $n$ copies of $\Delta^1$ along their initial vertex, so the $a_i$ give a simplicial cone with exactly the prescribed boundary and base $g$. This construction includes $n=0$: the quasi-inverse of the Segal equivalence to the one-point quasicategory supplies an apex over $[0]$.

source.place: Tuple construction supporting GH Proposition 3.4.5, using Definition 3.1.3 (Segal fibers) and Definition 3.1.10 (cocartesian fibration).

proof.text: For any specified cone $q$ over $g$, put $x=q(*)$ and $a_i=q(*\to i)$. Apply the limit dual of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test]. Since $I$ is discrete, its functor simplicial set and right-pinched mapping spaces are degreewise products, so the upper row of that test is $\operatorname{Map}(D,x)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Map}(D,v_i)$. If $p(D)=[m]$, its lower row is the map from the discrete set $\operatorname{Hom}([m],[n])$ to $\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}([m],[1])$ given by $\phi\mapsto(\rho_i\phi)_i$. The path pullback therefore has, over $\phi$, the fiber $\prod_i\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_i\phi}(D,v_i)$: paths in the discrete lower-right space force exactly these equalities. Homotopy fibers over a discrete space are the strict components indexed by its vertices. By [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection], with identity map on this discrete indexing space, the test square is a homotopy pullback exactly when all maps $F_q(D,\phi):\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}(D,x)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_i\phi}(D,v_i)$ are equivalences. This criterion applies to every $q$, without assumptions on its edges.

source.place: GH Remark 3.1.4 (mapping-space fiber calculation); constant-source relative-limit test, Kerodon 02X1, Proposition 7.1.6.19.

proof.text: If every $a_i$ is cocartesian, the second clause of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] says exactly that every $F_q(D,\phi)$ of Step 3 is an equivalence. Thus Step 3 makes every such specified cone a $p$-limit diagram. In particular this proves the relative-limit property for the exact-boundary cone $r$ constructed in Step 2; denote its apex by $y$ and its edges by $b_i:y\to v_i$.

source.place: GH Definition 3.1.3 and Remark 3.1.4, inert relative-limit condition.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $q$ is a $p$-limit diagram, with apex $x$. Step 3 gives equivalences $F_q(D,1_{[n]})$ and $F_r(D,1_{[n]})$ for every $D$ over $[n]$, with the same target $P(D)=\prod_i\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_i}(D,v_i)$. Surjectivity on components of $F_r(x,1)$ supplies an edge $h:x\to y$ over $1_{[n]}$ such that $[b_i h]=[a_i]$ for every $i$. Similarly $F_q(y,1)$ supplies $k:y\to x$ over $1_{[n]}$ with $[a_i k]=[b_i]$. Associativity of composition from [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] gives $[a_i k h]=[a_i]$ and $[b_i h k]=[b_i]$. Injectivity on components of $F_q(x,1)$ and $F_r(y,1)$ now gives $[kh]=[1_x]$ and $[hk]=[1_y]$. The inverse-triangle criterion in that same cited statement makes $h$ an equivalence. No restriction of a limiting cone to a smaller boundary has been used.

source.place: Converse comparison of two tuple apices using the fiber criterion of GH Remark 3.1.4; explicit inverse calculation in the homotopy category.

proof.text: By Step 1 the equivalence $h$ over $1_{[n]}$ is cocartesian. Fill the composable inner horn $(h,b_i)$. Its long edge $c_i$ is cocartesian by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Step 5 gives $[c_i]=[a_i]$. The composition statement [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] says that precomposition depends only on this component class, so $c_i$ and $a_i$ induce the same homotopy class of mapping-space square. Hence the cocartesian mapping criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] makes $a_i$ cocartesian as well. This proves the converse for every $i$.

source.place: Converse recognition of inert projections in the calculation supporting GH Proposition 3.4.5; composition and mapping criterion.

proof.text: For $n=0$, Step 2 already supplies an apex over $[0]$ and no edge data are required. For every specified apex over $[0]$, the second clause of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] applies with no chosen edges and says $\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}(D,x)\simeq *$ for every $D,\phi$. Thus the empty product case of Step 3 proves that every specified empty cone is a $p$-limit. All positive arities were covered above, and none of the arguments invoked ordinary limits, colimits, or presentability.

lean.statement: theorem inert_relative_tuple_cone {E : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory E] (p : E ⟶ monoidalSimplexBase.{u}) (hp : IsMonoidalInfinityCategory p) (n : ℕ) (g : leftJoinCone (∐ fun _ : Fin n ↦ (Δ[0] : SSet.{u})) ⟶ monoidalSimplexBase.{u}) (hg₀ : (orderedJoinInl Δ[0] (∐ fun _ : Fin n ↦ (Δ[0] : SSet.{u})) ≫ g).app _ (stdSimplex.obj₀Equiv.symm 0) = monoidalBaseVertex n) (hg₁ : leftJoinConeInclusion (∐ fun _ : Fin n ↦ (Δ[0] : SSet.{u})) ≫ g = SSet.const (monoidalBaseVertex 1)) (hgρ : ∀ i : Fin n, monoidalTupleEdge n i ≫ g = monoidalBaseEdge (monoidalRho i)) (v : Fin n → (monoidalUnderlying p) _⦋0⦌) : (∃ q : leftJoinCone (∐ fun _ : Fin n ↦ (Δ[0] : SSet.{u})) ⟶ E, leftJoinConeInclusion (∐ fun _ : Fin n ↦ (Δ[0] : SSet.{u})) ≫ q = monoidalTupleBoundary p v ∧ q ≫ p = g ∧ ∀ i : Fin n, IsCocartesianEdge p (monoidalTupleEdge n i ≫ q)) ∧ (∀ q : leftJoinCone (∐ fun _ : Fin n ↦ (Δ[0] : SSet.{u})) ⟶ E, leftJoinConeInclusion (∐ fun _ : Fin n ↦ (Δ[0] : SSet.{u})) ≫ q = monoidalTupleBoundary p v → q ≫ p = g → (IsRelativeLimitDiagram p q ↔ ∀ i : Fin n, IsCocartesianEdge p (monoidalTupleEdge n i ≫ q)))
lean.note: Exact prescribed-boundary existence and recognition for every cone over the specified inert base cone, including arity zero. The two helper definitions construct its canonical mixed join edges and prescribed boundary from the existing join and fiber inclusions.
